items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: I’ve had like for instance Bobby Watson, he once said to me, he said, “like I see so many white musicians being left behind, it’s not right,”

ctx.x: Is there any kind of racial thing happening in jazz right now that could be better?

Yeah. I think it definitely could be better. It’s not across the board, I think it’s just certain pockets of it. And I think in general it’s — the musicians have always been open minded They can hear, they can tell what’s going on. I mean I’ve had like for instance Bobby Watson, he once said to me, he said, “like I see so many white musicians being left behind, it’s not right,” and all that kind of stuff. And I mean they know what’s going on. And I don’t think — like white musicians I think feel very divided…

limited for black players. I mean there’s a lot of great black players from the 20s who like in the 30s were out of the music business and doing other things. So they had it rough. But the part that bothers me is just people who should be a little bit objective. I’m just bothered any time the focus is not on the music. Music should be judged on its own terms, not on racial terms. And I think one of the things I see happening is that jazz and the way it’s being marketed, by promoters, producers, club owners and…
